authority.decisionRecord: Pending operator merge after wrk.dog EIR soul review.

pomReviews.summary: Workspace-only evidence supports a revised plan, but the project remains assumption-heavy and must wait for operator validation.

research.summary: Workspace evidence shows a CivicState civic-letter product, not a Brooks History product. The repository contains application code, tests, Prisma models, API routes, worker agents, and planning docs, but paid demand, deliverability, official coverage, and legal-risk controls remain unvalidated.
sources: worker dispatch registry note and scrutiny list
methods: Read root and planning artifacts available in workspace-only mode.
Compared repository identity, package metadata, frontend copy, and planning docs.
Separated implemented code evidence from aspirational roadmap claims.
Built bottom-up market sizing from buyer count, usage frequency, and ARPU assumptions.
Stress-tested the plan through anti-plan risks: willingness to pay, deliverability, legal-adjacent citation risk, and official coverage.

planningMethod.evidenceHarvest: Preserved existing CivicState planning narrative and current code evidence while creating missing root soul artifacts.
planningMethod.marketResearch: No network research was available; all external market sizing and competitor claims are marked as assumptions in BUSINESS.md.
planningMethod.financialValidation: Revenue build reconciles paid submissions multiplied by assumed ARPU, with separate variable and fixed cost assumptions.
planningMethod.alternativeSearch: Compared manual constituent email, Resistbot, Change.org, LegalZoom-style document tools, Quorum, and VoterVoice as substitutes or incumbents.
planningMethod.antiPlan: Attacked the plan for nonpayment risk, government email deliverability, legal-adjacent citation liability, and local-official data coverage.
planningMethod.finalSynthesis: Keep CivicState on watchlist until paid beta, deliverability, official coverage, and legal-review load are measured.

segments.name: US residents with specific civic concerns
segments.painfulJob: They want government action but do not want to research jurisdiction, law, official contacts, formal letter style, delivery, and follow-up manually.

segments.name: Future civic organizations
segments.painfulJob: They may want repeatable civic letter workflows, but the repo explicitly defers organizational/API scope until the citizen pipeline is proven.

currentSubstitutes: Manual constituent email or phone calls.
Quorum and VoterVoice for enterprise advocacy teams.
Doing nothing because the research and routing burden is too high.
willingnessToPayEvidence: Paid demand is unvalidated [assumption: no revenue or traffic evidence in workspace].
The validation threshold is at least 3.0% preview-to-checkout conversion [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md].

market.category: Consumer civic-tech workflow for researched, cited, official-targeted constituent letters.
market.competitiveLandscape: Manual outreach, civic texting tools, petition platforms, document-prep tools, and enterprise advocacy suites solve adjacent jobs but do not prove CivicState's paid individual workflow.
market.wedge: Start with paid individual constituent letters and prove conversion, deliverability, official coverage, and citation safety before organizational expansion.

businessModel.valueCreation: Collapse the civic-action workflow from issue statement to researched, cited, official-targeted, delivered letters.
businessModel.valueDelivery: Web wizard, official lookup, AI research, citation verification, letter preview, Stripe payment, Postmark delivery, and dashboard/admin tracking.
businessModel.revenuePath: Beta paid submissions, then organic search and opt-in public campaign pages if paid conversion and deliverability gates clear.
businessModel.unitEconomics: Planning ARPU is $16 [assumption: tier mix], variable cost is $2.00 per paid submission [assumption], and gross margin before fixed costs is 87.5% [assumption].
businessModel.operatingCosts: DigitalOcean droplet at $96/month [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md], Mercury reserve of $1,500 [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md], and possible local-official provider cost of $100-$500/month [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md].
businessModel.marginLogic: Margins depend on low AI/email cost, low human review load, low chargebacks, and verified official data coverage.

financialModel.summary: The plan is a validation model, not a forecast: pilot revenue is $9,600 [assumption], proof-year revenue is $38,400 [assumption], and scale-year revenue is $153,600 [assumption].
financialModel.validationStatus: Needs operator and market validation; not approved for roadmap authority.
revenueAssumptions: Average revenue per paid submission is $16 [assumption: tier mix across $5, $15, and $25 packages].
Pilot year paid submissions are 600 [assumption: beta-to-launch volume].
Proof year paid submissions are 2,400 [assumption: repeatable SEO/social wedge].
Scale year paid submissions are 9,600 [assumption: 800/month run-rate target].
costAssumptions: Variable cost is $2.00 per paid submission [assumption: AI, email, queue, and support allocation].
Local official data provider may cost $100-$500/month [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md].
Scale-year fixed cost is $36,000 [assumption: support, monitoring, provider, and compliance reserve].
sensitivityTests: If ARPU falls to $8, scale-year revenue falls to $76,800 [assumption: 9,600 x $8].
If variable cost rises to $6.00, scale-year variable cost becomes $57,600 [assumption: 9,600 x $6.00].
If paid conversion is only 1.0%, the project fails the repo's 3.0% conversion gate [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md].

alternatives.name: Personal research asset
alternatives.thesis: Keep CivicState as a research/demo project until operator confirms it should pitch as a business.
alternatives.expectedUpside: Avoids overstating legal, market, and deliverability readiness.
alternatives.financialCase: $50,000 bear-band option value [assumption: research/tooling value, not revenue].
alternatives.rejectionOrSelectionRationale: Selected as the current default posture because registry notes say watchlist and not near-term investible.

alternatives.name: Transactional civic-letter business
alternatives.thesis: A low-price, delivered, citation-backed constituent letter may create paid individual demand.
alternatives.expectedUpside: $153,600 scale-year revenue in the current conservative model [assumption: 9,600 submissions x $16].
alternatives.financialCase: Gross margin can be high if variable cost stays around $2.00 per submission [assumption].
alternatives.rejectionOrSelectionRationale: Conditionally selected for validation, not for scale, pending paid beta and deliverability results.

alternatives.name: Organizational advocacy SaaS/API
alternatives.thesis: HOAs, nonprofits, or civic organizations could pay for repeat workflows.
alternatives.expectedUpside: Higher contract values than $5-$25 consumer packages [assumption: B2B pricing logic, not validated].
alternatives.financialCase: Deferred because the repo says third-party API/organizations require stable citizen pipeline first [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md].

antiPlan.summary: A skeptical partner would kill this unless paid conversion, .gov deliverability, local official coverage, and legal-adjacent safety clear measurable gates.

holes.hole: Users may like the preview but refuse to pay.
holes.whyItMatters: Without paid conversion, the product is a demo or public good, not a business.
holes.repair: Run paid beta and require at least 3.0% preview-to-checkout conversion [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md].

holes.whyItMatters: The core promise collapses if official-targeted emails bounce or land in spam.
holes.repair: Complete domain warming, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, bounce tracking, and suppression before broad launch [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md].

holes.hole: Legal citations increase liability and trust risk.
holes.whyItMatters: Incorrect or overconfident cited letters can be interpreted as legal advice.
holes.repair: Enforce citation verification, strip unverified citations, flag all-failed jobs, add disclaimers, and preserve human review.

holes.hole: Local official data may be incomplete or expensive.
holes.whyItMatters: Wrong or missing targets reduce user trust and may compress margins before volume exists.
holes.repair: Complete Cicero/BallotReady/local deferral spike before scaling GTM.

mitigations: Keep roadmap focused on validation instrumentation and operator gates.
Do not scale SEO until payment and deliverability gates clear.
Treat all external market claims as assumptions until network research and user evidence exist.
residualRisks: Official coverage may miss the repo's 95.0% federal/state and 60.0% local targets [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md].
Legal-adjacent review load may exceed one operator's capacity [assumption: launch operations risk].

strategy.diagnosis: The repo has a detailed CivicState build and codebase, but the business case is unvalidated and identity-mismatched with the brooks-history dispatch.
strategy.guidingPolicy: Validate the core paid civic-letter loop before adding distribution, organizational sales, or platform claims.
strategy.whereToPlay: US individual constituent communication for specific civic issues.
strategy.howToWin: Research, citation verification, official targeting, delivery tracking, and low-friction payment in one workflow.
strategy.moatHypothesis: Verified official directory, citation library, delivery history, and opt-in public campaign archive compound only after meaningful paid volume.
coherentActions: Resolve repo/project identity mismatch before investor publication.
Validate official lookup coverage and provider economics.
Keep legal-adjacent disclaimers and citation verification central.
tradeoffs: No subscription model in launch scope.
No organizational/API expansion until consumer loop works.
No claim filing, legal advice, or regulatory submissions.
No paid acquisition until organic and paid-conversion signals exist.

channels: Organic search from problem-specific civic queries.
Opt-in public campaign pages after safety and demand gates clear.
Social sharing from public campaign pages after launch validation.
assumptions: First beta cohort can recruit 25 prospects [assumption: operator-access estimate].
Organic search can reach enough civic-intent traffic [assumption: no SEO evidence in workspace].
Users will trust AI disclosure and citation-backed previews enough to pay [assumption: unvalidated].

jobs: Monitor failed citations and legal-adjacent edge cases.
Monitor deliverability, bounces, and spam complaints.
Maintain official-provider decisions and opt-out suppressions.
aiNativeAutomationTargets: Classifier for issue type and moderation routing.
Delivery agent for Postmark send state.
Treasury/reconciliation agent for ledger and payment checks.

aiWorkGovernance.wedge: AI-assisted civic letter workflow with mandatory verification and human review gates.
aiWorkGovernance.problem: Unbounded AI legal/civic drafting risks hallucinated citations, wrong officials, unsafe content, and overclaiming.
aiWorkGovernance.promise: Use AI only inside a constrained workflow: source-limited research, citation verification, moderation, audit logging, and operator review.
duplicatePrevention: Root BUSINESS.md is the current business authority.
Root ROADMAP.md lists buildable next work tied to BUSINESS.md headings.
DECISIONS.md records assumption-heavy items requiring operator validation.
tokenSpendControls: Tiered AI routing from repo plan.
Job-level budget authorization from repo plan.
aiWorkGovernance.risk: Legal-adjacent content remains sensitive even when framed as constituent communication.

regulatory: Not legal advice, not legal filings, not regulatory submissions.
CAN-SPAM compliance and opt-out handling are required in repo requirements.
AI disclosure is required in letters per repo requirements.
privacy: Political opinions and issue descriptions are sensitive user data.
Repo requires application-level AES-256-GCM for Tier 1 fields [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md].
CCPA/GDPR deletion process and data retention requirements are in scope.
security: Append-only audit and ledger HMAC checksums are specified and modeled.
Stripe webhooks, Clerk auth, and Postmark delivery require credential boundaries.
No production, spend, or credential authority is granted by this gate.
brand: Resolve Brooks History versus CivicState naming before wrk.vc publication.
operational: Workspace-only EIR pass used no external network research.

successMetrics: Government-domain inbox placement at or above 85.0% [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md].
Federal/state official coverage at or above 95.0% [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md].
Local official coverage at or above 60.0% [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md].
killTriggers: Paid conversion materially below 3.0% after beta [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md].
Deliverability materially below 85.0% after warming and provider fixes [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md].
Human review load makes the low-price model uneconomic [assumption: operational threshold not yet measured].
pivotTriggers: Users value drafts/research but not delivery.
Organizations show willingness to pay before individual consumers.
Deliverability blocks email-first model but research/drafting remains valuable.
reviseTriggers: WrkPlug shared-rails operator approval changes auth/billing posture.
External market research contradicts TAM/SAM assumptions.
Code verification shows roadmap-complete claims are overstated.
wakeConditions: Operator confirms whether this should pitch as a business despite registry watchlist note.
Paid beta and deliverability results are available.
